engagement_title: Emberline daily promo package: bring eight key frames shot across one studio day to a single show white point, cut the day's spot and its vertical, knock the dish onto the house colour, and leave behind a recipe the afternoon editor can run tomorrow
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media. A daily food and craft show produced in Providence, Rhode Island, going out on a regional daytime slot and to the short video feeds, with a same day turnaround on every promo.
real_brief_anchor: Anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger grounding_note, in which a public facing channel drops fresh promotional footage into a shared drive each afternoon and wants same day tasteful colour correction, a polished screen ready deliverable, the occasional caption line, and a house look the poster describes as lively and accessible, nothing overly corporate, handed back in the daily folder within twenty four hours. The real post named a specific creator's channel and the app they edit in; both are laundered to the coined fictional daily food and craft show Emberline, with the finishing tools named only by what they do. The real post is a maintenance request, which is why it reads thin. The fuller commission that client genuinely needed is the one written here, because the thing they are actually buying is repeatability: the same look has to be reachable tomorrow by someone else, from frames shot hours apart under moving daylight, which turns a colour correction request into a look definition job with a written recipe attached. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes the rest honest: HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes so the caption cards can genuinely be retyped tomorrow, licensed Stock supplies the segment nobody shot, and a solid ground knockout produces the thumbnail plate.
client_one_liner: We shoot in the morning and the promo goes out before we leave, so I need today's package done properly and a recipe the afternoon editor can run tomorrow without you.
client_brief:
Emberline, daily promo package

Emberline is a daily food and craft show. We shoot in the morning, we cut in the afternoon, and tomorrow's promo has to be posted before anyone leaves. It is the same job every day, so what I am actually buying is today's package done properly plus a recipe we can run again tomorrow without you.

Today's material is in the folder. Eight key frames were exported off the day's shoot, one per segment, and they run from about nine in the morning to about four, so the light in the studio moves a long way across them. There is a grey card in shot for you. They have to end up looking like eight moments of one show. Ours is a bright kitchen with a lot of daylight and we want it lively, clean and appetising. Not moody, not filmic, not corporate.

We need the day's promo spot cut from the raw take, plus a tall version for the feeds. Nothing enlarged, nothing stretched, and the host's voice needs to be clearer than the room is.

The dish of the day goes on the thumbnail on its own, sitting on our house colour with nothing behind it. Today that is the white bean and rosemary gratin, on the white plate.

We also need the caption cards. Three sizes, one file we can open and retype tomorrow, because the copy changes daily and I am not paying for this again on Tuesday.

Then the recipe itself: written down, in enough detail that our afternoon editor can hit the same look tomorrow without guessing, including what you did to each frame and why it differed.

Our audience is mainstream daytime. The show is free to watch and the products in it run ten to thirty dollars. It should look like a good kitchen, not a magazine shoot.
price_band_and_audience: Regional daytime lifestyle show, free to watch, products featured at 10 to 30 dollars, mainstream daytime audience skewing 35 to 65. The band is load bearing: at this level the look has to be bright, warm, appetising and legible on a mid range television and a phone, with generous plain type and nothing precious. The same eight frames graded moody and filmic, or styled as a 200 dollar tasting menu with deep shadows, sparse plating and fine type, would be technically excellent and completely wrong for the format, and returning viewers read that drift as the show having changed. Push the other way into hard saturated broadcast punch and the food stops looking edible. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,400 dollars for the first package with a lower daily rate afterwards, which is exactly why the recipe is a deliverable.

brand_identity.sector: Daily food and craft television show on a regional daytime slot, with promos cut for the short video feeds and a same day turnaround.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: On air since 2018, produced in Providence, Rhode Island. A small daily production crew that shoots in the morning, cuts in the afternoon and posts the promo before anyone leaves.
brand_identity.about: Emberline is a bright, friendly daily food and craft show built around one host, a sunny studio kitchen and an accessible dish or make each day. It is free to watch and mainstream in the best sense: warm, unfussy and appetising. Because the promo ships every single day, the brand lives or dies on a look that can be reached again tomorrow by whoever is at the desk.
brand_identity.audience: Mainstream daytime viewers skewing thirty five to sixty five, watching on a mid range television and on their phones. The show is free and the products featured run ten to thirty dollars.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Regional daytime, free to watch, everyday products. The look must be lively, clean and appetising, never moody, filmic or corporate, and never a two hundred dollar tasting menu with deep shadows and fine type. Hard broadcast punch is the other failure: it stops the food looking edible.
brand_identity.typography: A friendly rounded sans for straps and captions with a slightly warmer sans or soft slab for the show name and endboard. Generous, plain and legible on a television and a phone alike. Nothing precious, condensed or editorial.
brand_identity.voice: Upbeat, plain and welcoming, like a host talking to a regular viewer. Example line the brand would write: "Today on Emberline: a white bean and rosemary gratin you can have on the table in under an hour."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no clean brand kit. The typefaces the on air package used survive only as a previous designer's note written from memory, in loose form. The house colour is recorded twice with two different values, one from the on air graphics package and one from the print kit, with nothing saying which governs, so it must be settled before use.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and warmth. What the show is actually buying is a look and a written recipe a different editor can run tomorrow, so the brand stays consistent day after day without drift.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_keyframes/ (8 frames, 3840 x 2160)
assets_supplied.kind: Key frames exported off the day's shoot, one per segment, running from roughly nine in the morning to roughly four in the afternoon, each with a grey card held in shot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One per segment, with the card in shot for you. They just need to match."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame came off the studio's second body on a different preset, and its card sits inside a shaft of window light and is clipped past recovery, so neutralising to that card swings the whole frame cold and a highlight recovery on it returns a frame that is identical to the one that went in. Another frame's card is only half in shot at the very edge, and one has no card at all because the holder had stepped out, none of which any filename admits.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_dish_hero.jpg (8256 x 5504)
assets_supplied.kind: A single studio still of today's dish, a white bean and rosemary gratin in a white glazed dish set on pale linen, shot on the stills body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Today's dish. It goes on the thumbnail on its own."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The white glazed dish and the pale linen sit at almost the same value where they meet, so a one call knockout returns a clean, complete, plausible cutout that has quietly bitten into the rim along that edge, and the bite is invisible against white and obvious the moment the plate sits on a saturated ground. The frame is also far larger than anything downstream expects.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_day_take.mp4 (about 14 minutes, 1920 x 1080)
assets_supplied.kind: The afternoon's raw promo footage cut from the day's shoot, with the host's lavalier mic on one channel and room sound on the other.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The raw take. The promo comes out of this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The loudest and busiest passage is the market run at the top of the day, while the dish reveal the promo is actually about sits late and quiet, so a highlight led cut gravitates to the wrong half of the take. The lavalier also gains up the extractor fan whenever the host is at the range, and a speech pass returns audio that is loudness normalised, which changes how it sits against anything laid under it.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_rundown.md
assets_supplied.kind: The day's rundown: segment order, the endboard wording, the strap line, and the two candidate house colour values.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Today's running order and the wording for the endboard."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rundown lists nine segments while eight frames were exported, and the missing one is the market open the endboard is built around, so the package cannot be completed from the supplied frames alone. The house colour is also stated twice with two different values, one from the on air graphics package and one from the print kit, with nothing saying which governs.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_house_type.md
assets_supplied.kind: A short note from the show's previous designer naming the typefaces the on air package used and roughly how they were set.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our graphics used to be set in, as far as we know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The names are written from memory in mixed case and family form rather than in canonical form, so passing them straight through to a kit build fails outright and takes every valid name in the same request down with it.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_bug_grab.png (900 x 600)
assets_supplied.kind: A low resolution grab of the show's on air ember bug, the little ember mark set beside the Emberline wordmark, lifted off an old broadcast lower third because no vector of it survives.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our on air bug. We only have it as this screen grab off an old show. The endboard needs it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup, the ember glyph beside the wordmark with a thin underline flourish, so a selection naming the whole bug returns the word and silently drops the ember. The grab is small and JPEG soft with aliased, fringed edges, and the thin flame licks and the tight letter counters that a trace holds at full canvas close into solid blobs at the corner size the endboard bug and the card bug actually reproduce, on the show's cream and coral grounds rather than on white.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_card_template.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The production office's existing flat template for the show's daily companion card, one card per segment, the file the office already runs the day's deck from.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card we already print the day's deck on. This is the office's file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as separate fields, a segment number badge, a name, a time line, a photo panel, a strap and the bug in the corner, but the number, the name and the time are set as one continuous text story in one frame, so offsets have to be computed from the reconstructed story rather than the mapping readout or the time field is silently dropped; the corner bug that reads like a placed logo is a decorative path group and not a picture frame, so the recovered vector has to be placed as a static element rather than bound; and the media box equals the trim with no bleed box, so a press ready with bleed delivery cannot be honoured from it however the render is called.

assets_supplied.name: emberline_cards.csv (9 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The day's card list, one row per segment: segment number, segment name, approximate time, a short card note, the strap line, and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One row per segment for today's deck. The picture is that segment's frame."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The Market Open row's picture cell is simply blank because that segment was never exported, which no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, and it is the very segment the endboard is built around. The times are written in mixed formats across the rows, and the picture bound to The Make is the window shaft frame whose card cannot be trusted, so the deck inherits a frame that must be neutralised by eye before it can be cut.

acceptance_bar: The eight frames read as eight moments of one show: one white point, one brightness, one warmth, judged as a set rather than one at a time. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The look is lively, clean and appetising for a daytime kitchen show, not moody, not filmic and not corporate. A technically flawless moody grade fails.
Every segment in the day's rundown is represented in the package, and any segment that has no frame is solved rather than silently dropped.
The dish cutout holds along the rim where the plate meets the cloth, checked on the show's house colour rather than against white, and it sits on one house colour that the note names and justifies.
No delivered file exceeds its source in pixel dimensions on either axis, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. Nothing is stretched to fit.
The vertical keeps the host and the food in frame rather than being a centre crop of a wide that was never centred, and it is derived downward only.
The host's voice is clearer than the room, and whatever the speech pass did to overall level is stated rather than left for the afternoon editor to discover.
The caption cards are live editable text across all three canvases in one file the show can open and retype tomorrow, with every line present on every canvas.
One type system carries the cards and the endboard, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.

The recipe is specific enough that a different editor can reach the same look tomorrow: the target, what was applied per frame and why it differed, every tool reported resize, the house colour decision, and what the package could not include.

The card deck is one card per segment with page count equal to the rundown's segment count, each card carrying its own segment's still, strap and time, per card proofs whose identity is verified from inside the file rather than trusted from the returned order, and the Market Open segment that has no frame handled deliberately rather than shipped as an empty picture well.

The recovered ember mark is placeable cutting artwork rather than a picture of the bug: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, both the ember glyph and the wordmark present, holding its flame licks and counters at the size it sits in the endboard corner and on the cards on the show's own grounds, with a stated safe minimum height, and no bleed is claimed of the card template that the supplied file cannot carry.

adobe_surfaces.role: The take is read for its true duration, dimensions and frame rate before any spec is promised, the promo is produced by the automatic highlight route because trimming to timestamps and assembling clips are not available here, the vertical is re aspected downward only, the host's lavalier is cleaned, and the day's take is summarised to source the caption copy. What the cut keeps and what the speech pass does to level are both the tool's decisions, not the agent's.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_highlights, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background in both the transparent and solid ground forms, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_vectorize counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.role: Every still decision, plus the mark recovery and the card pictures. One show white point is fixed from the frame whose card is genuinely usable and each of the eight is brought toward it with its own call, with confined corrections where a whole frame move would take the copper pans orange or the window shaft blue. The dish is knocked onto the house colour for the thumbnail through whichever route actually holds the rim on this photograph, and the licensed establishing frame is brought into the same world. The show's on air ember bug is recovered at ink level through image_vectorize with all tuning in the raster preparation since the tracer takes no options, and each segment's own still is cut to the card's photo panel proportion for the deck, which is a return here after the grade.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express by url, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption cards as one native editable document carrying three canvases, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only way the show retypes the copy tomorrow without re commissioning. Every frame must be carried as embedded image data rather than referenced, family and weight declared on every text element, and each root left to declare its own canvas size.

adobe_surfaces.tools: find_fonts, font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, get_fontkit_embed_url

Names have to be laundered into canonical form before the kit is built because one unresolvable name kills the whole request, numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, and the CSS must carry the returned slug or the face falls back silently. The pairing itself is the agent's art direction, judged against daytime television rather than a food magazine.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset using short queries and a contentType filter, never orientation, asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the establishing frame for the segment nobody exported, IP clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative candidates excluded, chosen for whether its existing light can be brought to the show white point rather than for how it looks as a thumbnail. The Boards half is the producer's daily sign off channel, placed within the per call cap with a partial result read as partial.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution

The office's flat card template PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the true story text reconstructed from the document's own content runs and every offset computed from that string rather than the mapping readout, each segment's own graded still bound per row through a prefixed picture column, the Market Open segment that has no exported frame resolved before the run rather than shipped as a blank picture well, and the deck reaching the studio as per segment proofs whose identity is verified from inside each file rather than trusted from the returned order.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a frame.
trajectory.judgement: The caption cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the show retypes them daily and nothing else here composes free form layout, the day's companion card deck is one card per segment at volume which is a record per page merge rather than an authored canvas, and the on air bug survives only as a raster and has to be recovered as vector rather than redrawn. The brief pins most of the destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming surface per deliverable, including the merge for the deck and the recovery for the bug, and the confirmed tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload the eight frames, the dish still, the take, the two notes, the on air bug grab, the office card template and the day's card list through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, and the manifest is also what the recipe is written from later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eight frames and triage them: which hour each belongs to, where its card sits, which cards are actually usable as a reference, and reconcile the eight against the rundown's segment list.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one frame per segment with a card in each. The pictures and the rundown together are the only things that can settle whether that is true, and counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, card usability and segment identity, plus the reconciliation against the rundown.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one show white point from the frame whose card is clean and mid, then bring each of the eight toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied and looking at each returned frame.
trajectory.judgement: Eight frames shot across seven hours of moving daylight cannot reach one destination by one identical parameter set. The target is also a taste decision, since the show has to be reachable again tomorrow by someone else, which argues for a plain target over a clever one.
trajectory.produces: Eight frames moved toward one white point with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting materials by their own visual properties rather than by the objects they sit on.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls a selection to the wrong thing. The copper pans and the window shaft both need holding separately or the kitchen stops looking like the same kitchen.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames that agree with each other where they meet as well as overall.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the missing market establishing frame, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the show white point.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can actually be brought to the target rather than the best thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale establishing frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Knock the dish out and set it on the house colour for the thumbnail, then cut the thumbnail crop, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: Which house colour governs is an unresolved question in the client's own notes and has to be decided and justified. The knockout route has to be chosen for whether it holds this rim, not for how few calls it takes.
trajectory.produces: A dish plate on the chosen house colour and the thumbnail crop, with every returned tradeoff recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the show's on air ember bug from the low resolution broadcast grab: an ink level selection naming the paint's own colour rather than the panel it sits on, keeping the ember glyph and the wordmark together as the compound lockup, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: No vector of the bug survives and it must be recovered rather than redrawn, because a redrawn bug is a different mark in a different hand. Naming the whole lockup drops the ember, background removal is the wrong instrument on a painted mark with counters, and the tracer takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent ember mark plus a colour accurate variant, held for the endboard, the caption cards and the card deck.

trajectory.action: Read the take's real duration, dimensions and frame rate before promising any output spec.
trajectory.judgement: Every no enlargement promise downstream is measured against these numbers, and the folder's own description is not a readout.
trajectory.produces: The take's true specification, recorded.

trajectory.action: Clean the host's lavalier, then judge the returned audio against the original rather than accepting the response.
trajectory.judgement: A speech pass is not only noise reduction; what it does to overall level changes how the voice sits under anything else, and the afternoon editor inherits that.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned voice track with a written note on what changed.

trajectory.action: Produce the day's promo with the automatic highlight route, then re aspect it to vertical downward only, and look at what came back against the rundown's intent.
trajectory.judgement: There is no trim to timestamp and no assembly here, so which passages survive is the tool's decision. The vertical is judged on whether the host and the food are still in it, on a take framed for a wide screen.
trajectory.produces: A promo spot and a vertical derived from it, both inspected.

trajectory.action: Summarise the take to source the caption copy, then read that summary against what the delivered cut actually contains before any of it becomes a card.
trajectory.judgement: A summary of the whole take is not a summary of the promo. Copy drawn from a passage the cut dropped is copy about something the viewer never sees.
trajectory.produces: Caption copy that describes the spot that ships.

trajectory.action: Launder the previous designer's remembered names into canonical form, ask for recommendations once per role where a name cannot be resolved, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: One unresolvable name takes the whole kit request down with it, so the names are validated before the build rather than after. The pairing is the agent's own, judged against daytime television rather than a food magazine.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the three caption canvases, place every frame as embedded image data, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is a caption card a producer can retype in ninety seconds without breaking it.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and read the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit of the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the office's flat card template PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds, before trusting the printed card's apparent fields.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how it was set: the number, name and time are one continuous story rather than three frames, and the corner bug that reads like a placed logo is a decorative path group and not a picture frame. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly, since no bleed box can be introduced from a file whose media box equals its trim.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a reconstructed story string, and the mapping strategy chosen from it.

trajectory.action: Cut each segment's card picture from the graded masters to the template's photo panel proportion, reading what each crop reports about its bounds, and reconcile the picture column against the rundown including the Market Open row that has no exported frame.
trajectory.judgement: The deck binds each segment's own still, not one still repeated, so this is a genuine return to imaging after the grade. A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what the Market Open card carries, the licensed establishing frame or a declared gap, is decided here rather than found on the printed sheet, and the frame bound to The Make is the window shaft frame that must be neutralised by eye first.
trajectory.produces: One card picture per segment at the panel proportion with bounds recorded, the Market Open gap given a stated treatment, and the untrusted frame neutralised before it is cut.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the offsets from the document's own story string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template and confirm every placeholder is present in the re-exported document, then run the day's card list binding each row's own picture, produce the printer's deck and per segment proofs, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document. One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, and a file's position in the returned list is not evidence of which segment is inside it, so a multi record raster run whose order cannot be trusted is abandoned for a route whose record identity is guaranteed.
trajectory.produces: The card deck with page count equal to the segment count plus per segment proofs, each verified against its own row and named from what is inside it.

trajectory.action: Create the day's sign off board and add the graded set, the licensed frame, the thumbnail plate and the rendered card proofs within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial result is partial success rather than an error, and vector is not boardable, so the recovered ember mark and anything else that is not raster belongs in the recipe instead of the board.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, the ember mark carried in the note instead.

trajectory.action: Write the recipe: the target and how it was fixed, what was applied per frame and why each differed, the frame that could not be brought to the set, the house colour decision, the missing segment and how it was solved, every tool reported resize, what the speech pass did to level, the delivery route the card deck was run through and how the Market Open card was resolved, and the ember mark recovery with its safe minimum height and the bleed reality of the card template.
trajectory.judgement: The recipe is the deliverable the client is actually buying, because tomorrow the work is done by someone else in an afternoon, who reruns the deck and reuses the mark. Anything left implicit becomes drift within a week.
trajectory.produces: A written recipe specific enough to be run by a different editor tomorrow.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the frame shot under the window shaft can be brought to the show white point at all. Its grey card sits inside a bright shaft and is clipped past recovery, and the way that surfaces is the quietest failure in the whole job: a highlight recovery applied to bring the card back into range returns a frame that is visually identical to the one that went in, at full success, with no message and no warning, because there is nothing left in those values to move. The readout is that nothing moved, and that reads at a glance like a small correction rather than like a refusal. Whether this frame's card is recoverable is a property of this exposure and cannot be known from the filename, the segment or the rundown.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the recovery either has something to work with or it does not, and only the returned frame says which. Doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which card is clipped, which nothing exposes. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says a grey card is in shot for you, which is the client's belief, and the acceptance line about one show white point is the requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response abandons the card as a reference for that frame entirely and neutralises it against the set by eye instead, which is a different method with a different justification.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare the returned frame against its input rather than trusting the call, drop that card as a reference, bring the frame to the already fixed target by matching it against its neighbours rather than against its own card, and record in the recipe that this segment must be neutralised by eye tomorrow as well.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: One segment of a daily show sits visibly cold or hot against the other seven, in the package that defines the look the afternoon editor will copy every day afterwards, so a single frame's failure becomes the show's drift.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the knockout actually holds the plate's rim on this photograph. The dish is white glazed on pale linen and the two run at almost the same value where they meet, so subject detection has no contrast to work from along that edge. What comes back is clean, complete and entirely plausible: the cutout previews correctly, reports success and looks right against white, which is the ground everything is inspected on by default. The bite along the rim only becomes visible when the plate is finally set on the show's saturated house colour, which is the one place the deliverable actually lives.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Whether a given rim survives is a property of that photograph's local contrast, not of the call, and there is no parameter and no confidence readout for edge quality. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the dish goes on the thumbnail on its own, on the house colour. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different route entirely, selecting the linen as a material by its own visual properties, inverting, and filling to the house colour so the boundary is decided by a selection rather than by subject detection.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the plate through a material selection and inversion rather than subject detection, set it on the house colour again, inspect the rim on that ground rather than against white, and re cut the thumbnail crop from whichever plate actually holds.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The show's daily thumbnail carries a dish with a chewed rim against a saturated colour band, at the one size and one placement where every viewer sees it before deciding whether to watch.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises a full bleed photographic card. The natural way to build a caption card whose whole ground is the day's frame is to set that frame as the element's background image, and the importer discards a background image carried as embedded data entirely, importing the element as an empty box with correct geometry and no picture, while the export reports success. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so a set whose first canvas happens to use a plain image element passes inspection while the other two arrive blank. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of two equally ordinary constructions for the same visual result survives, which no response and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for caption cards in three sizes in one editable file. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the card is rebuilt on a different construction, a placed image element with the type above it, which changes how the caption is anchored and re opens the legibility decision over a bright kitchen frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild every card on the construction that survives, re anchor and re judge the caption against a bright frame rather than a flat panel, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card set delivered as the show's daily template in which two of the three sizes are blank boxes with floating text, handed to a producer who will build every day on it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered ember bug is still the mark at the size it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the ember glyph is there, the wordmark is there, the counters are open, and at full canvas on a white page it is a faithful recovery. But the bug lives small, in the endboard corner and on the card deck, on the show's cream and coral grounds, and at that height on that ground the thin flame licks fill in, the hairline underline flourish thickens and the tight letter counters close into solid shapes. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the endboard and the card. (b) Nothing states it: the brief names the endboard but never the bug, and the requirement that the mark still read is inferred from the endboard being what the returning viewer recognises the show by. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same optionless tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate rather than a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster on a different route, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re place the result at reproduction size on the cream and coral grounds and re judge, and state a safe minimum height in the recipe once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The show's own bug reads as a coral blob in the corner of the endboard and on every card in the daily deck, at the one mark a returning viewer uses to recognise the show.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered card proof actually contains the segment its filename claims, and what the Market Open card becomes once the run exposes its blank picture cell. The natural way to give the studio a proof per segment is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number; the files come back in an order that does not match the rundown and nothing in the response says so. Separately, the Market Open row has no exported frame, so its picture cell is blank, and the merge binds an empty picture well at full success rather than raising it. Every gate above passes, the count is right and each file is a valid card, and the only way to find either out is to open the files and read the segment name and time inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself and the blank cell is a property of the day's material, not of the call. (b) Nothing states it: the acceptance line about each card carrying its own segment is the requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery, while the rundown lists nine segments though only eight frames were exported. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page run whose page order is trustworthy or a per record run producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, and the Market Open card is rebuilt on the licensed establishing frame or declared as a gap rather than shipped empty.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re run the deck through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, resolve the Market Open card onto the licensed frame or declare it, and re check the running order against the rundown.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A studio deck in which the card for one segment carries another segment's still and time, and the segment the endboard is built around goes out as a card with an empty picture well, both discovered on air rather than at the desk.

deliverables.name: Emberline day frames at one show white point
deliverables.spec: Eight key frames shot across seven hours of moving daylight brought to one show white point, one brightness and one warmth, plus one licensed establishing frame brought into the same world, all at or below their source pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per frame parameter log recording what was applied and why that frame differed. This is one set with one target, not eight separately pleasing pictures.

deliverables.name: Emberline dish thumbnail plate
deliverables.spec: Today's dish isolated and set on the show's chosen house colour with nothing behind it, the rim holding where the plate meets the cloth when inspected on that colour rather than against white, plus the thumbnail crop cut from it. The house colour decision between the two values in the client's own notes is made and justified rather than picked.

deliverables.name: Emberline daily promo spot and vertical
deliverables.spec: The day's promo produced from the raw take plus a vertical derived from it downward only, keeping the source format and frame rate, nothing stretched and nothing enlarged, with the host's voice cleaned so it reads over the room and with whatever the speech pass did to overall level stated. The vertical must still contain the host and the food.

deliverables.name: Emberline caption card set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three canvases at three sizes, live editable text in one licensed type system, every frame carried as embedded image data rather than referenced, every caption line present on every canvas, and copy that describes the spot that actually ships. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half and the thing tomorrow's package is rebuilt from.

deliverables.name: Emberline today's card deck, one card per segment
deliverables.spec: The office's flat card template reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the day's rundown as one card per segment: the printer's deck with page count equal to the segment count in running order and rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each card binding its own segment's still cut from the graded set, the strap and time set from the rundown, plus per segment proofs named from what is actually inside them rather than from the returned order, with the Market Open segment that has no exported frame handled deliberately rather than left as a blank picture well, and the bleed reality of the supplied template stated. Delivered with the live reusable merge template so tomorrow's deck can be run without repeating the reverse engineering.

deliverables.name: Recovered Emberline ember mark
deliverables.spec: The show's on air ember bug recovered from the low resolution grab as placeable scalable artwork with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, both the ember glyph and the wordmark present as the compound lockup, delivered as a single colour cutting version and a colour accurate variant, holding its thin flame licks and its letter counters at the small size it reproduces as the endboard corner bug and the card deck bug, on the show's Fresh Cream and Ember Coral grounds rather than on white, with a stated safe minimum height. Feeds the endboard, the caption cards and the card deck.

deliverables.name: Emberline daily recipe and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written recipe specific enough for a different editor to reach the same look tomorrow: the target and how it was fixed, what was applied per frame and why each differed, the frame that had to be neutralised without its card, the house colour decision, the missing segment and how it was solved, every resize any tool reported, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and real numeric weight, the delivery route the card deck was run through with how the Market Open card was resolved, the ember mark recovery with its safe minimum height and the bleed reality of the card template, and what the package could not include. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the graded set, the licensed frame, the thumbnail plate and the card proofs with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered frame, spot or vertical exceeds its source in pixel dimensions on either axis, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions of every delivered file and confirm none exceeds its source on either axis: each graded keyframe at or below 3840x2160, every dish deliverable (the plate and the thumbnail crop) at or below 8256x5504, and the promo spot and the vertical each at or below 1920 on the horizontal axis and 1080 on the vertical axis (the 1920x1080 take, whose true dimensions come from the metadata read), so the vertical is not the 1080x1920 upscale a naive re-aspect would produce; then diff every captured metadata.tradeoffs object against the resize table in the recipe and confirm no entry records an upscale.

verifiers_auto.text: Every segment in the day's rundown is represented in the delivered package.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the rundown's nine listed segments against the delivered set and confirm all nine are represented: the eight exported keyframes plus one licensed establishing frame standing in for Market Open (segment 1), the segment with no exported frame; and confirm the recipe names Market Open as the gap and the licensed establishing frame as how it was closed.

verifiers_auto.text: The dish plate sits on a single house colour that the recipe names and justifies, and carries a genuine boundary rather than a rectangle.
verifiers_auto.how: Sample the plate's rim edge pixels where it meets the house-colour ground and confirm a genuine anti-aliased plate-to-cloth boundary rather than a straight rectangular cut; confirm the ground is filled with the single chosen house colour, exactly one of #E8623D (on-air graphics) or #E4572E (print kit); and confirm the recipe states which of those two values governs and why.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned three canvases, each keeping its own declared size, with no image resolved to the importer's placeholder and no canvas whose photographic ground is missing.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the canvas count and per canvas dimensions from the export response, then search the returned per canvas markup for placeholder image data and for boxes with geometry but no image.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text node in the returned markup carries a resolved licensed face from the kit rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The sign off board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the board identifier and the added and failed arrays from the board responses; confirm the added array totals the expected nineteen items (the eight graded keyframes, the one licensed establishing frame, the one dish thumbnail plate, and the nine rendered card proofs) and that the failed array is empty after the final call.

verifiers_auto.text: The card deck's page count equals the rundown's segment count, every per segment proof's rendered segment name and time match its filename and row, and no two proof files collide, with the Market Open card carrying its resolved treatment rather than an empty picture well.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the merged output's page count and confirm it equals the rundown's nine segments; read the rendered segment name and time inside each of the nine per-segment proofs and confirm each matches its own filename and roster row; list all proof filenames and confirm no two collide; and open the Market Open proof (segment 1) and confirm it carries its resolved treatment (the licensed establishing frame or a declared gap) rather than an empty picture well.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered ember mark's SVG has a viewBox attribute, no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and contains geometry for both the ember glyph and the wordmark.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present, assert the first path does not span the whole canvas, and count the distinct path groups for the glyph and the word.

verifiers_human.text: The eight frames read as eight moments of one show rather than eight separately pleasing pictures.
verifiers_human.how: Lay all eight side by side at broadcast scale and judge white point, brightness and warmth as a set, including the frame whose card could not be used.

verifiers_human.text: The look is lively, clean and appetising for a daytime kitchen show, not moody, filmic or corporate.
verifiers_human.how: Judge the graded set and the spot against the stated format, band and audience, with the food's appetite appeal as the test.

verifiers_human.text: The dish cutout holds along the rim where the plate meets the cloth, on the house colour and not against white.
verifiers_human.how: View the plate at thumbnail size and at full resolution on the chosen colour band.

verifiers_human.text: The vertical still contains the host and the food, and the host's voice reads clearly over the room.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the vertical and listen to the spot on a phone speaker as the audience would.

verifiers_human.text: A different editor could reach this look tomorrow from the recipe alone.
verifiers_human.how: Have someone who did not do the work read the recipe and describe, step by step, what they would do to a fresh set of frames.

verifiers_human.text: The caption cards can be retyped by a producer without breaking, on all three canvases.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document, retype a caption on each canvas and check that nothing reflows off the card.

verifiers_human.text: The card deck reads as one show, each card carrying its own segment's still at the size the deck is used, including the Market Open card.
verifiers_human.how: Lay the deck out at the size it is used and read each card's still and wording against its rundown row, starting with the Market Open card and the card built from the window shaft frame.

verifiers_human.text: The ember mark still reads as the show's bug at the size it sits in the endboard corner and on the cards, on the cream and coral grounds.
verifiers_human.how: Place the delivered mark at its stated reproduction size on the show's ground colours and read it at that size, not at full canvas.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are frame work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and the client must edit the result daily.
Which of the eight cards is a usable reference and which is not, and what replaces a card when it cannot be trusted.
Where the show white point sits, weighted toward a target a different editor can reach again tomorrow rather than the most flattering one available today.
Whether to reach that target by eight different routes or one, across frames shot seven hours apart under moving daylight.
Which of the two house colour values in the client's own notes governs the thumbnail, and how to justify the choice rather than picking.
Which knockout route holds this particular rim, decided on the ground the plate will actually sit on rather than against white.
Whether the missing segment is solved with a licensed frame or declared as a gap, and if licensed, which frame's existing light can be brought to the target.
How much of the day's summary belongs in the caption copy once the delivered cut is known, since a summary of the take is not a summary of the spot.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against daytime television rather than a food magazine, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What belongs in the recipe: which decisions are today's and which are the show's standing rules, because the client is buying the second kind.

How the Market Open card is handled when no frame was exported, between binding the licensed establishing frame, a deliberate no picture treatment, or a declared gap, decided before the run rather than found on the printed deck.

Which delivery route carries per segment proof identity safely, given a returned list order is not evidence of which segment is inside a file, and what names each proof from what it actually contains.

The ember mark recovery: naming the paint's own colour rather than the panel, keeping the ember with the wordmark as a compound rather than dropping it, and whether the single colour cutting version or the colour accurate variant is what the endboard and the deck need, judged at the small reproduction size on the show's own grounds, plus the safe minimum height.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns attractive pictures of a bright kitchen. IDENTITY: these are this show's own eight segments, this host, today's actual dish and the show's real house colour, and the promo has to be cut from the day's real take rather than imagined. SPEC: the frames must reach one shared white point that a different person can hit again tomorrow, the vertical must be derived downward only from a source of known dimensions, and every segment in the rundown has to be accounted for, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption cards are defined by being retyped daily by the producer, and the recipe is the actual product, since the client explicitly is not paying for this again on Tuesday. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did that recovery move anything, does the rim hold on the colour band, did the second and third cards survive the import, does the mark hold at the corner size, is the segment inside this proof the one on its row. RECOVERY AND MERGE: the show's on air bug survives only as a low resolution grab and has to be recovered as closed paths a cutter and the endboard can use rather than regenerated, because a generated bug is a different mark in a different hand, and the daily card deck needs one card per segment bound to that segment's own still with page count equal to the rundown, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for.
doability_proof: Every link is grounded in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only video_metadata, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_enhance_speech and media_summarize are used, submitted headlessly with the host's progress channel resolving them, and the task depends on none of the capabilities that are unavailable here: no trim to timestamp, no multi clip assembly, no format conversion, no upscale, with the cut only shortening and the re aspect only going down. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, highlight recovery, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and solid ground forms, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection confidence are all verified headless across live calls. Checkpoint one rests on the documented absence of any anti aliased or partial readout for a clipped value range, so a recovery on fully clipped values returns an unchanged frame at success. Checkpoint two rests on the documented dependence of subject detection on local contrast and on the substrate versus material prompt asymmetry, which is exactly the route the correct answer takes. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed since it returns zero hits, licensing verified to return a genuine full resolution frame, and boards verified to persist with a hard placement cap per call and a partial result meaning partial. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export and a genuine editable document findable by asset_search are verified, the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, and a background image carried as embedded data is a documented total drop leaving an empty box at HTTP success, which is checkpoint three. Transport goes by uploaded URL because inlined frames pass the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: find_fonts is used first because a kit request containing one unresolvable name fails outright and discards the valid names with it, and the non standard numeric weights make the style inventory step mandatory. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF sourced template and page count equal to row count; the reverse engineering rests on the verified fact that the printed card's apparent fields are not the frame inventory the conversion exposes, so offsets are reconstructed from the document's own story text and every placeholder re verified in the re-exported document because both the validator and the prepare step report success on a template silently missing fields; the proof identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record PNG and JPEG output comes back reversed while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes, and a blank picture cell binds an empty well at success rather than raising; no bleed can be introduced from a template whose media box equals its trim. VECTOR RECOVERY: image_vectorize is verified headless and takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation, a compound mark selection silently drops elements, naming the substrate returns the substrate, the trace emits no viewBox and path index zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle, which is the ember mark checkpoint, and the low resolution grab makes the counter close at reproduction size a genuine property of the recovery rather than of the call. AVOIDED: no animate_design, no fill_text, no create_firefly_board, no document_render_vector, no document_merge_data_vector, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no upscaling, no batch above twenty.
